subject: Throughput validation + pricing bands for Dedicated GPU pool (Nova Inc)
messages:
From: Ava Cole <ava.cole@novainc.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: procurement@novainc.com; Daniel Ortiz <dan.ortiz@novainc.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput validation + pricing inquiry for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production LLM feature and need a clear sizing + pricing proposal we can take to procurement. High-level details:
- Model: custom Llama2-70B variant (int8 quantized in prod)
- Typical request: ~512 tokens input, 256 tokens output average
- Traffic profile: baseline ~50 TPS, daily peak bursts up to ~200 TPS (~90th-95th percentile traffic windows)
- Latency target: p95 < 150ms for user-facing generation

Can Redwood run/validate a load test on our behalf (or provide current internal benchmarks) showing expected TPS and p95 for a Dedicated GPU pool? Also need proposed commit sizing and a pricing band for 12/24-month commits (we're sensitive to committed discounts).

Procurement (cc'd) will want an estimate they can model into the FY27 budget. If possible please include: recommended GPU-equivalent pool size, expected sustained TPS, headroom for bursts, and a few pricing options.

Thanks —
Ava
Ava Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Nova Inc
ava.cole@novainc.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Ava Cole <ava.cole@novainc.com>
Cc: procurement@novainc.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput validation + pricing inquiry for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Ava —

Happy to help. We can run a controlled load test that mirrors your traffic profile and produce TPS/latency curves plus traces/dashboards. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we run tests so we size correctly:
- Is your model running with KV cache enabled for interactive sessions?
- Do you have batching tolerance (i.e., can you accept ~3–10ms batching delays to increase throughput)?
- Expected sampling config (top-p/top-k, temperature) — this changes latency.

Prelim notes based on similar workloads: for ~200 TPS peak at ~512/256 seqs, you'd typically be in the 3–5 A100-equivalent range (or 1–2 H100s with SLO-aware batching and quantization). With continuous batching + prefix/KV caching we often see +15–25% TPS vs naive runs.

Propose: we run a 2-phase load test this week — (1) baseline steady-state at 50/75/100 TPS for 30m each; (2) burst tests to 200–240 TPS with realistic arrival patterns. Deliverables: CSV TPS report, p50/p95/p99 latencies, representative traces, and a recommended commit size + pricing bands.

If you confirm the KV/cache/batching details, I'll schedule the run and target delivery in 48 hours.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
From: Ava Cole <ava.cole@novainc.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Daniel Ortiz <dan.ortiz@novainc.com>; procurement@novainc.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput validation + pricing inquiry for Dedicated GPU pool

Thanks — answers inline:
- KV cache: yes, we will enable KV cache for interactive sessions (session affinity exists).
- Batching tolerance: up to ~5ms avg added latency OK for cost savings, but anything beyond that starts to affect UX.
- Sampling: top-p=0.92, temp=0.8, nucleus sampling, n_candidates=1.

Budget context: procurement is asking for comparison between (A) a 12-month committed throughput contract and (B) a 24-month longer commit. They're looking for an example pricing band (approx %) so they can run an NPV.

Please proceed with the run; we'll need the artifact for internal review.

—Ava
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Ava Cole <ava.cole@novainc.com>
Cc: procurement@novainc.com; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput validation + pricing inquiry for Dedicated GPU pool

Ava — attaching the results from the run we completed this morning. Deliverables attached: redwood_tps_report_20260721.csv, traces_20260721.zip, and a one-page draft quote (draft_quote_nova_20260721.pdf). Also shared a drive folder with dashboards: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nova-loadtest-20260721

Summary (short):
- Test config: model approx. Llama2-70B-int8, seq_in=512/seq_out=256, KV cache enabled, batching window 5ms
- Sustained results (observed):
  • 4x A100-equivalent pool (continuous): sustained ~180 TPS, p95 = 165ms, p99 = 240ms
  • With aggressive batching + kernel optimizations (same hardware): peak observed 210 TPS, p95 = 148ms, p99 = 210ms
  • Single-shot cold-starts add ~30–40ms to first-token in some flows (see traces).
- Recommendation: commit to a 4x A100-equivalent pool with a 10% burst buffer (i.e., baseline commit = capacity for 200 TPS, burst up to 220 TPS). This gives production p95~150ms in the optimized configuration.

Pricing bands (indicative list price assumptions):
- Option A (throughput-priced, 12-month commit): reserve 200 TPS equivalent capacity — list monthly = $78,000. 12-month committed discount: 8% => $71,760/mo.
- Option B (throughput-priced, 24-month commit): reserve 200 TPS — list monthly = $78,000. 24-month committed discount: 15% => $66,300/mo.
- Option C (capacity-priced, 12-month commit with 4x A100 reserved nodes): list monthly = $75,000. 12-month discount: 10% => $67,500/mo. 24-month discount: 18% => $61,500/mo.

Notes on structure: we can do throughput-based billing (easier for traffic variability) or node-based reserved pools. Throughput-based is more predictable for Nova's use case (bursts are smoothed in the SLO policy). Final pricing will depend on exact SLA terms (p95 targets and included burst headroom).

I've labeled these numbers "indicative" — Marissa, Karthik: can you review the discount bands and SLA text?

Thanks, attaching artifacts.

--
Rishi
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Throughput validation + pricing inquiry for Dedicated GPU pool

Ava — great to see the numbers. A few operational notes from our side:
- We can commit to the recommended 4x A100-equivalent pool with an SLA that targets p95 < 160ms for the optimized config. Production SLA (p95 <150ms) is achievable after a 2-week tuning window and a short pilot; we'll include remediation credits if SLA misses are due to infra faults.
- For procurement: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month at the 12-month discounted rate if Nova signs a 12-month deal within 30 days. For 24-month deals, we can extend the onboarding credit and a 5% additional discount on the first 6 months.
- Please include Security in the loop for SOC2 evidence. Rishi, I'll attach the SOC2 RoC to the final quote if needed.

Karthik — can you confirm the suggested discounts are within our current pricing grid and whether we should route a special exec-approval for the 24-month 18% figure Marissa referenced?
